rule: An atom imports no other tier.
why: An atom that imports another tier is arranging children. It is a composite with the wrong name.

rule: A frame may import an atom only to place an element the frame itself owns — a divider between children, for example. Test: is the imported thing something the caller handed in? If yes, the frame is doing a composite's job.
why: A frame never hand-rolls what an atom already owns, and never reacts to what its children are.

rule: A frame does not reach upward.
why: A frame reaching upward is reacting to content it must not know about.

rule: A composite arranges its atoms inside frames.
why: Hand-rolling flex at composite level puts the same spacing decision at every call site.

rule: A composite does not know a domain.
why: A composite that knows a domain entity is a block, whatever folder it sits in.

rule: A page names blocks and feeds them typed data.

why: A page reaching two tiers down usually means a block is missing, and the shape it builds inline is invisible to every other screen that will need it.

rule: Vendor components are wrapped at the bottom and never imported above it.
why: A block importing a vendor component lets that vendor's constraints leak into domain code, and the house system can no longer constrain it back.
